subject: Is stacking data possible for within year-different month observations?

messages.author: 7595ad705c6bb0b8
messages.subject: Is stacking data possible for within year-different month observations?
parts:
Hello everyone,

I have a question regarding a bird species data set and the possibility of it being analyzed to obtain N (abundance) for an area. I know the routes this could be done in unmarked: "gdistsamp", "occuRN", "pcount"; each follow specific models from their associated articles.  To summarize the information:

- Method: fixed-radius point count
- Sites 178
- Visits 3 (but these visits were spread out in 1 year time: first visit january, second visit march-april, third visit jun-jul) 

This is a resident bird species which remains within the geographic area and although it is not certain if it disperses due to little information available (as some species might do in search of food), we didnt see a real difference in contacts per bout (they were pretty equal). I believe the species remains within the surveyed sites. However, the assumption that the population is closed cannot be met because sometime during the year their would be a breeding season, so there would be births and deaths in a year-cycle.

From what I have encountered in the group, people have had a similar situation where they survey in multiple years. The suggestion in these cases has included "stacking the data"

Would this be something I could do? I think that the advantage that other people have is that they have their three or more visits per year so if they stack the data they have replications per site, in my case stacking the data would result in 1 count bouts, correct?

Thanks in advance for any comment, suggestion or direction to authors/materials. And thanks to all users and authors in this group, it is definitely different from other groups, I have learned a lot in the past few weeks from the questions, answers, suggestions and articles recommended.

Best

Fabiola R

messages.author: e191b485fda719b3
messages.subject: Re: Is stacking data possible for within year-different month observations?
parts:
Fabiola,

Other folks can chime in here, but I think for at least pcount, IF you are willing to assume that births and deaths occur at equal rates across sites, you can still assume closure (Seber 1973).  That's a pretty big assumption depending on your sites and research questions, but the value of repeated surveys at each site will really strengthen your results if you think you can honestly make the assumption above.  If your sites differ by some covariate like habitat type, I THINK you could extend the assumption to equal birth and death rates within a habitat type provided your models account for habitat type.  But I'd be curious if others would agree with that statement.

-Alex W.

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Is stacking data possible for within year-different month observations?
parts:
hi Fabiola,
 I assume you used a normal point count protocol and NOT distance sampling or time-removal or similar.
 In that case , due to the long time span of the counts, the population is certainly not closed in this time.
 You could fit the Dail-Madsen model (pcountOpen in unmarked) but note this is a pretty advanced model and very sensitive to sparse data and the specific model assumptions that underlie it. You should do a lot of reading on the model and proceed cautiously.
 
regards,
andy

Let me follow-up with a direct answer to your question:
 
Stacking the data is a great solution to dealing with non-closure without modeling explicit dynamics. BUT you still need some replicate counts which, by my understanding, you don't have.....

messages.author: 7595ad705c6bb0b8
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Is stacking data possible for within year-different month observations?
parts:
Hello all,

Noted. 
 
Distance (meters) to individual was taken as we wanted to assess when we'd stop detecting the individuals, as well as to know what would be our circular plot limit to take some vegetation structure and composition metrics to characterize the habitat. We also recorded the first interval of detection to assess if our 10 minute count is OK or if less would suffice for future surveys. But, unfortunately we did not keep "ticking" interval boxes if an individual remained throughout the counts, records are based on first-contact only. So I believe that this is what you mean when you mention time-removal, correct?

Thank you for your responses. All part of the learning experience for sure. 

Fabiola R.
El lunes, 5 de octubre de 2015, 8:25:40 (UTC-6), Jeffrey Royle escribió:
Let me follow-up with a direct answer to your question:
Stacking the data is a great solution to dealing with n on-closure without modeling explicit dynamics. BUT you still need some replicate counts which, by my understanding, you don't have.....

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Is stacking data possible for within year-different month observations?
parts:
Dear Fabiola,
 Since you have distance then I would recommend the use of the gdistsamp() function which accommodates such repeated distance sampling data.
 In addition, you should definitely buy the forthcoming book
http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/0128013788?keywords=kery%20and%20royle&qid=1444062381&ref_=sr_1_1&sr=8-1
 which has almost 200 pages written on various types of hierarchical distance sampling models including "open" models.
regards
andy
